         1                  Recently I had a very successful

         2       and compelling hearing on the issue of clergy

         3       abuse and abuse by those in positions of

         4       power.  We had very, very compelling testimony

         5       from victims, but we also had testimony from

         6       experts, academics and attorneys and

         7       professors of law, all of whom agreed that

         8       merely by extending or eliminating the statute

         9       of limitations would we then be able to

        10       pinpoint perpetrators and allow victims of

        11       abuse to have their day in court.

        12                  So I'm pleased that we're doing

        13       this bill, which extends the statute of

        14       limitations.  But we also have a

        15       responsibility to extend the statute of

        16       limitations so those who have been victimized

        17       can have their day in court and we can stop

        18       the victimization of any more persons by

        19       people in a position of authority.

        12                  SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:    Thank you,

        13       Mr. President.

        14                  I rise in support of this bill,

        15       called the Bill Leaf-Brandi Woods bill.  And

        16       basically we've had two tragedies in Central

        17       New York very recently, where Bill Leaf, a

        18       reporter for WSYR, in his twenties, and Brandi

        19       Woods, a 15-year-old Girl Scout, delivering

        20       Girl Scout cookies -- not much older than the

        21       children that are here in the gallery today --

        22       were both killed by drunk drivers.

        23                  In the Brandi Woods situation, the

        24       perpetrator received a one-to-three sentence

        25       and is about to be released.  The other case


                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.

         1       is still pending.

         2                  Two fine people.  Bill Leaf was

         3       here reporting in Albany a couple of days

         4       before his death, a rising reporter, an

         5       incredible young man who was going to be

         6       national someday, there's no question.  Brandi

         7       Woods, a young girl doing the right thing with

         8       a Girl Scout troop, just a life snuffed out.

         9                  Well, the penalties for DWIs,

        10       especially repeat offenders, were woefully

        11       inadequate, as can be seen by the sentence

        12       that the first individual got, in the Brandi

        13       Woods case.  This bill intends to address

        14       that.

        15                  And I would hope that we would have

        16       unanimous support for this bill, because it

        17       increases penalties for people who have been

        18       convicted before of driving while intoxicated

        19       or driving while ability-impaired when they

        20       either seriously injure someone or kill them.

        21                  And I think by passing this bill --

        22       and the Assembly sponsor is pushing to pass

        23       the bill as well -- that we can send a message

        24       out that it's not going to be tolerated.  And

        25       even if you're not a major drinker, if you


                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.

         2       have a very bad result, injuring somebody

         4       jail.  And you're going to jail for a long

         6                  There should be no more Bill Leaf

         7       and Brandi Woods stories.  And hopefully a

         8       bill like this would help that occur.

         9                  So I vote aye, and I urge all of my

        10       colleagues to unanimously support this

        11       extremely important piece of legislation.
